newsitem.title: MADAGASCAR: Madagascar votes in presidential runoff.
newsitem.headline: Madagascar votes in presidential runoff.

text.p: The people of Madagascar voted in a runoff presidential election on Sunday and former Marxist military ruler Didier Ratsiraka was widely expected to defeat ex-president Albert Zafy.

The vote in the Indian Ocean island republic was called after Zafy, 69, elected to succeed Ratsiraka in 1993, was impeached by parliament in July for abuse of his authority and exceeding his constitutional powers.
Zafy had earlier won a referendum empowering him, rather than parliament, to appoint the prime minister.

Politicians and straw polls predicted victory for Ratsiraka, who returned from 19 months of voluntary exile in France at the end of September, after a campaign that aroused little excitement. Officials forecast a low turnout.
None of the 15 candidates in the first round in November won enough votes to secure outright victory.
Ratsiraka led the first-round poll with 36.6 per cent of the vote, against 23.4 per cent for Zafy.
His prospects improved when millionaire businessman Herizo Razafimahaleo, his former economic adviser who took 15.1 percent of the vote in the first round, threw his party's support to Ratsiraka.

Sale of alcohol was banned for the day, and observers from Francophone African countries were monitoring the polls, due to close at 6 p.m. (1500 GMT). Full results were not expected for several days because of poor communications in many areas.
The strength of support for Ratsiraka, a 60-year-old retired admiral, surprised many political analysts.
He was reviled by many of his people in the early 1990s for using the army to resist the pro-democracy movement in Madagascar, where most of the population of 14 million live in chronic poverty.
His ousting in 1993 followed a wave of political protest which virtually paralysed the country for many months.

Diplomats said the optimism that marked Ratsiraka's ousting had evaporated in the political squabbling after Zafy took over, and many people apparently thought they would be better off with Ratsiraka back in office.
